course_name_en: Refrigeration, Air Conditioning, and Heat Pump Technology 1
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics, especially: understanding of fundamental thermodynamic and fluid mechanical principles and laws

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire a fundamental understanding of thermodynamic processes and heat transfer in refrigeration and heat pump systems, as well as associated storage systems.
Understand the physical principles, components, and functionalities through theoretical instruction, independent calculations, and accompanying laboratory experiments.
Students design, calculate, and analyze processes and systems in this context.
They independently solve specific problems and critically question the application and significance of the technologies.

syllabus_topics: Refrigerants and their environmental impacts (local and global)
Components of refrigeration systems and heat pumps
Classification of thermal storage systems according to physical principles
Areas of application and motivation for use
Thermodynamic principles: operating principles, material data, and heat transfer
Sensible heat storage with water and solid media
Latent heat storage: phase change materials and ice storage systems
Integration and operating strategies of thermal storage systems in plant engineering
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a 120-minute written examination.
